title: Pranit Lanjewar, MSW, LSW
text:
Hello! I’m Pranit Lanjewar. I am a licensed social worker, specializing in adult mental health and trauma-informed care. My professional experience includes homelessness, mental health, healthcare, community-based practice for social change, and currently in social work academia.
I aim to pursue a Ph.D. in the near future, with a research focus on mental health and cancer. I also have many hobbies that rotate with the seasons; to mention some, biking, writing, walking, running, cooking, reading, gaming, socializing, and going on road trips.

title: Full Publication List
text:
These research papers focus on key international perspectives on homelessness. These two papers examine how systems and communities define homelessness and how that definition differs across countries. We have discussed systemic issues, community perspectives toward homelessness, programs and services available, and potential approaches to reduce homelessness in those countries. We discussed how the community can contribute to this solution. These papers were prepared through a literature review, comparative studies, interviews, qualitative research methods, analysis, and collaboration between me and neuroscientist/clinical social worker/Licensed Independent Clinical Dependency Counselor, Dr. Richard Romaniuk. |

title: PranitLanjewar
text:
Some voices wish to be heard, not seen.


I often express myself through blogs. My blog name is Unspoken; it refers to someone who feels unheard, wants to express how they feel about anything, and still wishes to remain unseen. Someone who wants their thoughts, emotions, experiences, and opinions to be heard without having to reveal who they are.
---
Falling off!
In a space full of chaos and tragedies, one is looking for peace. The division holds value, and the people stand, narrating stories. An overwhelming cult has its own shade that is enough to cover the transparency and take you away from reality! Yes, I’m veering off the path that could have led me to the darkest side of positivity. Words lost their meaning, commonly taken for granted, and created their own language. Yes, falling away from the perspectives that are impactful and submissive to new language, definitions, eras, etc. Assumptions are profound; delusions are believed, yet feel stronger than ever. Maybe it’s just the new me, making my way to the worst without cognizing potential effects. Or maybe I simply normalized chaos as it is now a part of living……………..!!!!!!!!
- Unspoken
